result.target_topic: Company Business Model and Manufacturing Scope
result.target_summary: Intel operates as a global designer and manufacturer of semiconductor products, including CPUs, primarily marketed through its Intel Products business and manufactured via Intel Foundry operations and external suppliers. The company seeks to expand its Intel Foundry business to serve external third-party customers.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: Both disclosures define Intel's core business structure as a global designer and manufacturer of semiconductors (CPUs and solutions). 2023 D001 establishes the 'global IDM' status, while 2024 D001 updates this to 'global designer and manufacturer' and explicitly mentions the Intel Foundry operations and external customers, reflecting the strategic evolution of the same business model.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global Technology Scope and Product Portfolio
comparisons.peer_summary: Avago is a global technology leader designing semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, including AI networking, home connectivity, and software for mainframe and cloud platforms, while also offering fibre channel storage area networking products.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose their core identity as global semiconductor designers and manufacturers (AVGO explicitly as 'designs, develops and supplies'). They similarly outline the breadth of their product portfolios targeting key infrastructure sectors. Intel emphasizes its design and manufacturing scope including CPUs and foundry services, while Broadcom details its broad range of semiconductor devices and infrastructure software for enterprise, data center, and connectivity markets.

sentences.text: We are a global designer and manufacturer of semiconductor products, including CPUs and other solutions, primarily marketed and sold through our Intel Products business and manufactured via our Intel Foundry operations and other suppliers.
We are a global technology leader that designs, develops and supplies a broad range of semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions.
We develop semiconductor devices with a focus on complex digital and mixed signal complementary metal oxide semiconductor based devices and analog III-V based products.

We offer thousands of products that are used in end products such as enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence ("AI") networking and connectivity, home connectivity, set-top boxes, broadband access, telecommunication equipment, smartphones and base stations, data center servers and storage systems, factory automation, power generation and alternative energy systems, and electronic displays.

peer_results.rationale: Micron's disclosed candidates focus on industry market conditions (weak demand, pricing changes, China regulatory impact) rather than the company's fundamental business model, product scope, or organizational strategy. Disclosures about macroeconomic headwinds and market cycles are not comparable to a disclosure defining the company's core business operations and manufacturing design scope.

comparisons.peer_topic: Impact of Export Controls on China Revenue and Product Strategy
comparisons.peer_summary: Sales to China dropped from 19% of Data Center revenue in FY2023 to 14% in FY2024, with mid-single-digit representation in Q4 FY2024 and Q1 FY2025 expected. Nvidia has not received licenses for restricted products, is shipping small volumes of alternatives, and is expanding its portfolio to offer solutions that do not require licensing.
comparisons.comparison: While Intel's disclosure focuses on its general business model and foundry expansion strategy, NVIDIA's disclosure highlights how its product strategy is constrained and shaped by external regulatory factors (export controls). Both disclose aspects of their product portfolio and market exposure, but NVIDIA's specific focus on China revenue dynamics and licensing restrictions represents a distinct operational driver compared to Intel's internal manufacturing and foundry scope description.

sentences.text: We seek to expand our Intel Foundry business as a third-party foundry for external customers.
Our sales to China decreased as a percentage of total Data Center revenue from 19% in fiscal year 2023 to 14% in fiscal year 2024.
We are working to expand our Data Center product portfolio to offer new solutions, including those for which the USG does not require a license or advance notice before each shipment.
We have started to ship alternatives to the China market in small volumes.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm operates through three reportable segments: QCT (semiconductor), QTL (licensing), and QSI (strategic investments), along with nonreportable segments like QGOV.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose their organizational structure and primary business activities within their Item 7 MD&A. Intel defines its scope as a global designer and manufacturer marketed through specific business units (Intel Products and Foundry). Qualcomm similarly details its organization into specific reportable segments (QCT, QTL, QSI) that define its primary semiconductor and licensing businesses.

sentences.text: We are a global designer and manufacturer of semiconductor products, including CPUs and other solutions, primarily marketed and sold through our Intel Products business and manufactured via our Intel Foundry operations and other suppliers.
We are organized on the basis of products and services and have three reportable segments.
We conduct business primarily through our QCT (Qualcomm CDMA Technologies) semiconductor business and our QTL (Qualcomm Technology Licensing) licensing business.
